name: AI Energy Boom
description: Hypothesis scenario: no effective demand cap on energy — AI compute and robotics have near-unbounded appetite. Levers vs baseline: datacenter/robot ceilings lifted an order of magnitude (60,000 TWh / 3,000 per 1000 workers) and the AI cognitive labor payoff on (aiWorkerEquivalentPerTWh 1e5). FINDING (round-2 review): in this model the binding constraint is NOT the capex-budget share — the savings pool (~$600T/yr) dwarfs energy capex (~$10-30T/yr), so cleanShareFlex is inert and was removed from this scenario. Financing binds instead through the COST OF CAPITAL: WACC rises to ~15% by 2075 as automation, energy buildout, and CDR compete for savings (K/Y compressed to ~1.8), raising LCOE and slowing the transition. The remaining ~4k TWh shortfall reflects physical diffusion/penetration ceilings, not money. Result (2026-model): GDP 2100 ~$2,800T, generation ~740k TWh, warming ~2.7C. Sustained real rates >12% and K/Y <2 are outside anything observed — read the financing dynamics as qualitative. Uncalibrated hypothesis, not a forecast.
